clue.text: Rubber bird I replaced by middle of May

indicators.note: one thing replaced by another means a single letter is swapped out for a new one
the middle of a word is its central letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a sandpiper is a long-billed wading bird
taken as written; this is the letter that goes
the central letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: Someone describes a rubber duck-like toy bird, altered somehow by springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the I of SANDPIPER for A to get SANDPAPER. 'Rubber' here is something that rubs, not the elastic material.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive paper is used to rub surfaces smooth, so it is literally a thing that rubs.

clue.text: Maybe Joey to leave motor racing track unexpectedly

blocks.note: first meaning: Joey was a sitcom that followed on from Friends, an example of a derived series
second meaning: a car that loses grip may rotate and slide off the circuit

explanation.surface: A young kangaroo, a joey, seems to want to flee a racing circuit without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: A joey is a baby kangaroo, which is the reading the surface pushes; here it is the TV show Joey, a follow-up to Friends. As a verb phrase the answer is 'spin off'.
explanation.definitionFit: A derived television series built around a character from an earlier show is called by this term; Joey is an example.

clue.text: Gossip about one being more smart

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: to natter is to chat idly
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gossip about someone who thinks themselves cleverer than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' suggests cleverness, but here it means well dressed. To natter is British for chatting at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neatly and stylishly dressed, so the comparative describes someone better turned out, which is smarter in appearance.

clue.text: Vietnamese soup’s super when condensed, essentially – it reacts with proteins

indicators.note: the essence of a word is taken to be its very centre, so only the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup, with the possessive S
slang for excellent
as in 'as I arrived'
the fifth of nine letters

explanation.surface: A foodie praises a reduced Vietnamese broth before a sudden swerve into biochemistry.
explanation.walkthrough: PHAT is street slang meaning great. The surface reads 'condensed' as describing reduced soup; only its central letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosphatases are enzymes that strip phosphate groups from molecules, including many proteins, so they act chemically upon them.

clue.text: Marsupial droppings covering car with roof removed

indicators.note: in a down entry the roof is the top letter, and taking it off drops the first one
to cover something is to go around it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: a childish word for excrement
motor is an informal word for a car

explanation.surface: Some animal has left its droppings all over a convertible.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a convertible, but in a down entry the roof is the first letter, so only that comes off. Motor is an old-fashioned British word for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The potoroo is a small Australian rat-kangaroo, a pouched mammal, so it is one example of the class.

clue.text: Managed two-thirds of schedule, showing animosity

indicators.note: keeping two parts in three means the final third of the word is cut away

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
a course of treatment is a schedule of doses

explanation.surface: A manager got through most of the timetable but with obvious hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: COURSE has six letters, so two-thirds is its first four.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name deep, lasting bitterness and ill will felt towards another person.

clue.text: Best comedian with shaved head

indicators.note: shaving the head takes off the top, which for a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: someone hilarious is called a scream

explanation.surface: Praise for the top stand-up comic, the one with the bald look.
explanation.walkthrough: A scream is an informal term for a very funny person; lose the S.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, as in the cream of the crop, the top selection.

clue.text: Short, elegant letter from Athens

indicators.note: a short version is cut down, here by dropping its final letter

blocks.note: chic means stylish

explanation.surface: A brief, stylish note posted from the Greek capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests correspondence, but it is a character of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is the twenty-second character of the Greek alphabet, used in writing in Greece.

clue.text: Jules, possibly, probing alien hypothetical communication infrastructure

indicators.note: a probe goes inside something, so one piece is pushed into another

blocks.note: Jules Verne, the French science-fiction writer; 'possibly' marks him as one example of a Jules
the extraterrestrial of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A science-fiction writer investigating how aliens might theoretically talk to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Jules Verne, a pioneer of science fiction, fits the alien theme neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The evernet is a proposed always-on network linking every device permanently, a speculative future version of the internet.

clue.text: In error, dispatch young woman with object

blocks.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly sends off a girl along with some item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' suggests a thing, but it means a goal, as in 'to that end'.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix mis- means wrongly, so this verb is to send something to the wrong place by mistake.

clue.text: Right bores enthusiastic about prelude

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so one piece is pushed inside the other

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Tedious people get excited about the overture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' reads as a noun, dull people, but it is a verb meaning drills into.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction or opening passage comes before the main work, just as a prelude precedes the larger piece.

clue.text: Piquant quality of Moroccan dishes including new spices, primarily

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside
primary means first, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: tagines are slow-cooked North African stews named after their conical pots
the standard abbreviation
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A food critic praises the sharp flavour of North African stews thanks to fresh spices.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'of' as part of a food review; it simply joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something piquant has a sharp, pleasantly stinging flavour, and tang is exactly that zesty taste.

clue.text: Autobiography shows charm

indicators.note: to show something is to put it on display, and the letters are on view inside a longer word

blocks.note: the third to fifth letters

explanation.surface: A memoir reveals its writer's charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' suggests charisma, but it is a magic token. OBI is a less common spelling of obeah, Caribbean folk magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi or obeah is a West Indian form of sorcery, and the word also names a fetish or amulet used in it.

clue.text: Mere end-of-year claptrap at work, or a good way to reward staff?

definitions.text: a good way to reward staff?

indicators.note: something at work is being operated on and changed, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: all twenty-one letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A cynic dismisses the office's year-end bonus speeches as nonsense, then wonders if that might be the fairest system.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the whole phrase, hyphenated words included. The question mark hedges whether such schemes are really good.
explanation.definitionFit: Linking wages or bonuses to measured output is a common scheme for rewarding employees according to results achieved.

clue.text: Having many locations, University claims millions put off

indicators.note: something off has gone bad or wrong, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
taken as written
the standard abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A university with sites everywhere says it has postponed millions in spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' reads as postponed, but 'put' is fodder and 'off' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution spread across several separate sites or grounds is described this way, especially universities and colleges.

clue.text: Medley of writing, perhaps, in distant past

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: writing is one of the three Rs; 'perhaps' marks it as an example
far ago means long since

explanation.surface: An anthology of old writings from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, the basics of schooling; each can give R.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble or hotchpotch of things, which is what a medley is.

clue.text: See 12
Fish arrive in bays?

blocks.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
to land is to come in to arrive

explanation.surface: Fish come in to the coastal inlets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bays' suggests the coast, but bay is the laurel tree, whose leaves are woven into a victor's wreath; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath of laurel or bay leaves was the traditional crown for poets and victors, a circular decoration.

clue.text: She wrote request to block setter, 50

indicators.note: something that blocks sits in the way, wedged inside

blocks.note: a gel sets, as jelly does
to ask is to request
the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler of fifty pleads for something to be stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'setter' is not the crossword's compiler but something that sets. Elizabeth Gaskell wrote Cranford and North and South.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Gaskell was a Victorian English novelist, so she is a woman who wrote.

clue.text: Swimmer cut my back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: to dock a tail is to cut it short
cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their back has been injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation, not the possessive; cor is the British equivalent, like 'gosh'. 'Swimmer' in crosswords often means a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock cod is a fish found among reefs and rocky coasts, so it is one kind of aquatic creature.

clue.text: Methodist urban housing muddle

indicators.note: a thing that houses holds something within it, so the letters are inside the phrase

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A church's city accommodation programme is in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing' looks like a noun about homes, but it is a verb meaning containing.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddle papers is to throw them into disorder, just as disturbing them moves them out of place.

clue.text: Laboured like some circus performers?

blocks.note: first meaning: stiff and unnatural, especially of speech or writing
second meaning, playful: raised up on tall poles, as clowns often walk

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second sense is whimsical: performers who walk on tall poles could be said to be so equipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboured prose is forced and awkward, and the adjective describes stiff, artificial style; it literally means mounted on long poles.

clue.text: Performed song on the counter for drink

indicators.note: counter means against or opposite, so the letters run the opposite way

blocks.note: a singer performs by singing
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A busker sang standing on the bar top to earn a free drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' paints a bar top, but counter means contrary.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine, fruit and spirits, served as a cold beverage.

clue.text: Better assistant is trendy sort with time for husband

indicators.note: 'with X for Y' means put the first in place of the second, a swap of letters

blocks.note: a hipster follows the latest fashions
the standard abbreviation
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A superior aide turns out to be a fashionable type who keeps their husband waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective, but it is someone who bets; a person who sells racing advice helps them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster offers predictions on races or matches, which helps someone placing wagers decide where their money goes.

clue.text: Senior member cooked nurses bread in Japan

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold closely, as a baby in arms, so one piece cradles another

blocks.note: food that is ready is done
bread is slang for money, and the yen is Japan's currency

explanation.surface: An elder of the household baked and lovingly looked after the bread on a trip to Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' as money is old slang; the surface keeps it in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected or longest-serving woman in a group or profession, its most senior figure.

clue.text: Annual ritual rearranging ten car seats

indicators.note: to rearrange is to put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Every year someone shuffles the seating in a big people carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a family's yearly road trip; the answer is an office Christmas custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Each Christmas, colleagues draw names and give anonymous presents; this custom recurs every year.

clue.text: See 12
Former revolutionary with brief question for Treasury department

indicators.note: a brief version is cut short, losing its final letter

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born guerrilla
a query is a question

explanation.surface: An old rebel has a quick question for the finance ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: Che Guevara is the crossword's favourite revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the Exchequer is the government's account and the office managing public revenue, part of HM Treasury.

clue.text: A number going naked the day before

indicators.note: naked means stripped of covering, so the outer letters come off

blocks.note: seven is one example of a number

explanation.surface: A song-and-dance routine performed nude the night before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' tempts as a song or act in a show; it is a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The eve of an event is the evening or day immediately preceding it, as in Christmas Eve.

clue.text: Overturned tennis umpire’s call for Don

indicators.note: something overturned is flipped upside down, so the order is inverted

blocks.note: in tennis 'not up' is called when the ball bounces twice before being hit

explanation.surface: A tennis umpire's decision about a player named Don was reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: Don reads as a man's name, but it is the verb meaning to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to dress in them, which is exactly to wear them by getting into them.

clue.text: Make stick shelter

blocks.note: first meaning: to wedge something so it becomes stuck fast
second meaning: a small house or cabin, or to give someone a room

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a noun for a branch, as if building a hut, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A bone can become wedged in the throat, and a gatehouse or cabin offers a place to stay.

clue.text: One in women’s underwear going to the right restaurant

indicators.note: moving rightwards means a letter shifts later in the word and is set back in further along

blocks.note: the full name of the bra
the Roman numeral for one; it is the letter that moves

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a bra heads off to the right towards a café.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of BRASSIERE and set it back two places on, after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style eating place serving simple dishes and drinks, a kind of eatery.
